messages.author: 44b2d0363580cfa7
messages.subject: Latent Growth Curve Lavaan vs MPlus very different results
parts:
Hello,
I am trying to replicate a model created by a colleague in MPlus with lavaan and am getting very different results. The regression estimates especially bear almost no resemblance to the MPlus results. Can anyone figure out what might be causing this?

Here is my lavaan code
mod2 <- '
i =~ 1*t1 + 1*t2 + 1*t3 + 1*t4 + 1*t5
s =~ 0*t1 + t2 + t3 + t4 + 1*t5
t1 ~~ 0*t1


i ~ domStratRA + domStratRD + 0*nStrats + reachOut
s ~ domStratRA + domStratRD + nStrats + 0*reachOut
'


fit2 <- growth(mod2, data=dfFull, mimic = "Mplus")
summary(fit2, fit.measures = T, rsquare = T)


Here is the Mplus code:
i1 s1| t1@0 t2*1 t3*1 t4*1 t5@1;
t1@0;

i1 on domStratRA              
      domStratRD              
      nStrats@0
      reachOut
;
s1 on domStratRA              
      domStratRD              
      nStrats
      reachOut@0
;

Shouldn't these two models be equivalent? Why might I be getting such drastically different results?

messages.author: 99a06696c483481a
messages.subject: Re: Latent Growth Curve Lavaan vs MPlus very different results
parts: Your lavaan code does not set start values for the free slope loadings, while the Mplus code does. Given the marginal ID status, that could make a difference. Try adding start(1) modifiers to set starting values.

messages.subject: Re: Latent Growth Curve Lavaan vs MPlus very different results
parts:
I am getting EXTREMELY different results though. I think there is a major issue at play. I have one hypothesis I would like to get your thoughts on please.
But first some more details. 
domStratRA and domStratRD is a three category variable ("R", "D", "A") coded into 2 dummy variables with "R" as the reference. nStrats contains integers between 0-3. reachOut is a binary yes/no variable (coded as 1/0).

I seem to be having the biggest problem with the domStratRA/RD variables. There are numerous NAs in those vectors. If I have lavaan imputing missing cases for the t1-t5 variables via the "mimic = mplus" variable, is it also going to try to impute values in the domStratRA/RD variables? I feel like that could be causing the mistakes. I think the correct course of action would be to not include NAs in those regressions. For instance, if a case has a domStrat of "D", then their domStratRA variable would be NA and it wouldn't make any sense to impute a value there. Is that what lavaan is trying to do though?

messages.subject: Re: Latent Growth Curve Lavaan vs MPlus very different results
parts:
Lavaan or Mplus are not "imputing". To do the model with Multiple imputations you need to use the runMI function in semTools

Could it be that Mplus is using FIML to handle missing data (their default), and you are using listwise deletion on lavaan? set the argument missing="fiml" in lavaan to use FIML. Also, you can check in the output from each program if they are using the same number of observations. Fi they are using differnet number of observations they are handling missing data in different ways

Can you share the output from both programs? That is needed to see the differences

parts:
Ashish

lavaan doent impute data, to do imputations you have to set up with the runMI function.

It seems they are both using Full Information Maximum Likelihood (FIML), this never generates imputed values.
